text: The Bladespire Keg King was an ogre that was once found at an ogre camp on the Vortex Pinnacle in the Blade's Edge Mountains. He was removed in patch 2.1.0 when that camp was replaced by Ogri'la, being himself replaced by the Ogri'la Keg King. He had a debuff that caused player characters to get drunk.
Bloodthirst Blade technically drops from Kha'damu in during the Blood Moon event, but cannot actually be looted as it is Unique (0).

Brann's Epic Egg has a chance to spawn from Brann Bronzebeard during combat after reaching level 5 which unlocks the talent for the Healer and Damage specalizations, while the tank spec has it at level 9. After short time or the player destroys it, it spawns a Devilsaur which acts as a guardian pet for a short time. Mechasaur EZ-Build Kit causes the egg to hatch a Mechasaur instead.
Cenarion Storm Crow are druids in storm crow form located in Zangarmarsh and the Blade's Edge Mountains.
Champion's Spear is a warrior class talent. It grants the Champion's Spear (2) ability while active.

Chestguard of Wrath is part of the Unstoppable Wrath set, the Tier 2 tanking armor set for Warriors. It can be purchased from Victor Nefriendius in with Primeval Chest. It can be traded to Duke Hydraxis in the for a "" version, which has the same stats but is part of the Immoveable Might set.

Crunching for Cultists is a feat of strength earned by winning 50 rounds in the Twilight's Blade Strategem game at the Twilight Ascension basecamp. It is a tic-tac-toe mini game. Enchant Weapon - Oathsworn's Tenacity is created with Khaz Algar Enchanting (20); taught by Enchanting trainers in Khaz Algar for . Amount of Versatility granted depends on the quality of the enchant.

The Evil Koi-Koi is an arakkoa ghost that appears in a scripted event at Evergrove in the Blade's Edge Mountains after turning in The Truth Unorbed. In the event, a residual memory from within the Orb of the Grishna shows a Grishna Arakkoa summoning the Evil Koi-Koi to possess an Unsuspecting Leafbeard.
Fear Whisperers were shivarra that used to spawn at Forge Camp: Terror in the Blade's Edge Mountains. They were removed in patch 2.1.0 when daily quests were added to the area.
Fel Ragers were entropic elementals that used to spawn at Forge Camp: Wrath in the Blade's Edge Mountains. They were removed in patch 2.1.0 when daily quests were added to the area.
Ferocious Idol teaches the Mangle rune for leg armor. In order to use this item, you must first use abilities that cause bleed effects against humanoid mobs 20 times while the Idol is equipped.

wielding Fyr'alath in concept art.]] Fyr'alath the Dreamrender is a 2-handed axe obtained from the Amirdrassil, the Dream's Hope raid. It is a strength weapon and only death knights, paladins, and warriors can use it. After collecting numerous resources from across the Dragon Isles, the axe was forged by Igira in Zaralek Cavern for Fyrakk, enchanted by Druids of the Flame, infused with Smolderon's essence, and imbued with shadowflame. It allowed Fyrakk to open tears into the Emerald Dream, hence its name.

The Garb of the Shadowmoon is an 8-piece cloth armor transmog set. The set can be purchased from at the Dwarven Bunker and from in the War Mill garrison building. It takes 490 Iron Horde Scraps and the 3 armor tokens to get the full set of 8 pieces.

Mana-Debt Slaves are slaves of the Bash'ir ethereals in the Blade's Edge Mountains. A Bash'ir Arcanist will occasionally call several of them in to realign the Bash'ir Crystalforge at Bash'ir Landing. Two of them can also be found wandering around the Crystal Spine with the Bash'ir Surveyor.
Metal Shield is an ability used by a pet during a Pet Battle.

The Mo'arg Extractor is a mo'arg that can be found patrolling the westernmost plateau in the Blade's Edge Mountains, along with 2 Crystalfused Miners. They will spawn at either Forge Camp: Terror, or Forge Camp: Wrath and will patrol towards the Vortex Summit. There, they will stop at 2 spots, where they will attempt to mine the crystals in the area. After that, they will head back to the forge camp they came from, where they will despawn. Upon reaching the mining spots, this mob will cast a fear on any wildlife that is nearby.

Tier sets, often shortened to simply tier, are class-specific armor sets that traditionally drop in raids. Tier added since patch 9.2 can also be obtained by converting other equipment at a catalyst. These sets offer powerful set bonuses and a unique visual appearance for each class. The related term raid tier describes a group of raids that drop loot around the same item level. Tier sets may be spread across different raids within the same raid tier; for example, the shoulders may drop in one raid and the chestpiece may drop in another.

Armor Points are a statistic in XCOM 2 that determine how much damage is reduced on a unit before it takes damage to its Hit Points. Both Soldiers and Aliens can have Armor Points. Yellow pips to the right the Health bar represent Armor Points, available on select suits of armor and certain abilities. Any incoming damage, except for Armor Piercing (armor-ignoring) damage, will be reduced by this amount, applied before the Armor is shredded. Armor is only depleted when shredded and will otherwise continue to offer full protection. Soliders can receive Armor Points by equipping certain Armors or speccing into select abilties, whereas Aliens have Armor Points innately.

An interceptor is a combat aircraft deployed by XCOM to engage and shoot down UFOs that have been detected by satellites in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Individual interceptors are stationed in regional airbases and are only capable of launching sorties against UFOs detected over that continent.

The Plasma Blaster is a Heavy Weapon in XCOM 2. Like all heavy weapons, it can only be mounted on heavy armors or SPARK and has 1 ammo charge per mission. This weapon is very similar in function to the Psi Operative's Null Lance ability, and should be used similarly. The Plasma Blaster will fire a large plasma blast in a straight line 1 tile wide (3 if used by a SPARK with the Rainmaker perk) and 25 tiles long, piercing all targets. It deals high damage, and will ignore 4 armor points. It is useful for dealing damage against armored pod leaders and taking out support troops in the process.

The Hellfire Projector is an heavy weapon in XCOM 2. Like all heavy weapons, it can only be mounted on heavy armors or SPARK and has 1 ammo charge per mission. As an upgrade to the Flamethrower, this weapon is similar in function. This weapon fires a cone of flames with a wide spread that deals high damage to those within and inflicts them with Burning. Flame will cover all tiles affected by the weapon, which cause burning to those that move on them. Icarus Jump is an ability granted by the Icarus Armor. Icarus Jump allows the soldier to move to any visible tile within a certain range. Use of Icarus Jump will remove Concealment. It receives two charges per mission and has a 2-turn cooldown.

The Katana is a secondary weapon in the War of the Chosen expansion for XCOM 2. It is the signature weapon of the Chosen Assassin. The Katana is the most powerful melee weapon available to XCOM. While it has no status secondary effect like the Arc Blade or Fusion Blade, the Katana deals more damage, ignores up to 5 armor on the target, and attacks cannot miss or graze the target, meaning it will always deal full damage.

Resistance Armor is a class of Armor unique in appearance and wearable only by soldiers of Resistance factions in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. The Temple Ship serves as the mothership for the alien invasion and houses the Uber Ethereal, leader of the Ethereal collective in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. This massive ship appears off the coast of South America immediately after XCOM successfully raids the Overseer ship and brings the Ethereal Device back to base. The Temple Ship's arrival sends seismic shock waves across the planet. Too large (and likely well armed) for any conventional assault even by XCOM's advanced interceptors, it remains unassailable until the Volunteer activates the Gollop Chamber and makes contact with the Uber Ethereal.

Weapon Upgrades (also called weapon mods, or, simply, mods) are available for all primary weapons of soldiers in XCOM 2's campaign after researching Modular Weapons. Weapon upgrades can be acquired as random loot drops in a mission, bought from the Black Market, or obtained from the rumor sites. A primary weapon may take 1 such upgrade with the first tier. All primary weapons receive a second mod slot at the second tier. If the 'Armed to the Teeth' Continent Bonus is acquired, an additional upgrade slot per primary weapon becomes available, up to a maximum of 3. Accuracy Up is a Blade Art in . It grants the Driver a buff that increases accuracy by 25% for 15 seconds. This effect persists across Blade Switches. The AC Accuracy Up Arts Card grants Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ access to this Blade Art, with cooldown that varies with equipment rank. The effect power of this art can be boosted using Board Game Pouch Item effects, increasing accuracy by up to 50% at maximum. The duration of the buff can be extended up to 22.5s with the effects of the Helping Hand Aux Core or Skill RAM.

Absorb Damage is a Blade Art in . It grants the Driver a Damage Barrier buff that nullifies up to 10% of his maximum HP in damage. The effect has no duration and persists across Blade Switches. After the cumulative amount of damage is absorbed the barrier dissolves, leaving the Driver vulnerable once again. The AC Damage Absorb Arts Card grants Poppi α and Poppi QTπ access to this Blade Art, with cooldown that varies with equipment rank. The effect power of this art can be boosted using Board Game Pouch Item effects, increasing the barrier's maximum HP up to 20%.
